clue.text: European organ eclipsing a Beyoncé record

indicators.note: to eclipse is to hide something by passing in front of it, so the newspaper's name swallows the next word

blocks.note: Le Monde is a French daily newspaper, and a newspaper is often called an organ
taken as written

explanation.surface: A European body part somehow blots out one of Beyoncé's albums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' tempts you towards body parts, but here it means a publication: LE MONDE with A tucked inside gives LEMONADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is the title of Beyoncé's acclaimed 2016 studio album, so it is one of her records.

clue.text: See nothing up with Mark dropping round

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from the bottom, so it runs backwards
to drop something is to let it go, and a round thing is the ring-shaped letter, which is removed

blocks.note: nil means nothing, as in a football score
a colon is a punctuation mark

explanation.surface: An instruction to look upwards at nothing while someone called Mark sheds a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese. Reversed NIL gives LIN; COLON losing one O gives COLN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is a cathedral city and the seat of an Anglican bishop, so it is a see, a bishop's diocese.

clue.text: Hormone you get from fruit, staying at home

indicators.note: something staying in a place is lodged inside it, so the small word sits within the fruit

blocks.note: a melon is a fruit
taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A health claim that a hormone can be obtained by eating fruit while staying indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staying' looks like part of the surface, but it tells you the small word lodges inside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Melatonin is the hormone produced by the pineal gland that regulates sleep cycles.

clue.text: Older relative from northern Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from the bottom upwards, so the town's name runs backwards

blocks.note: Annan is a town in Dumfries and Galloway, south-west Scotland

explanation.surface: A grandmother who comes from a town in the north of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern' looks like a description of the town, but in a down clue it means read upwards; ANNAN backwards gives NANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is an affectionate name for a grandmother, a relative of an older generation.

clue.text: Mother nature undermined by extremely lowly insect

indicators.note: in a down entry, being undermined means having something placed underneath, so the next piece follows below
extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
one's self is one's essential nature
the first and last letters of lowly

explanation.surface: Mother Nature being sabotaged by a very humble bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother nature' reads as one familiar phrase but splits into two pieces; in a down clue, undermined means the last piece sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: A damselfly is a slender insect related to the dragonfly, folding its wings at rest.

clue.text: One mushroom without more or less white top?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the mushroom sits around the abbreviation

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcini
ca is short for circa, meaning approximately

explanation.surface: A single mushroom, roughly speaking, with a pale white cap on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside. The question mark flags the definition as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: An icecap is the permanent white covering of ice on a mountain summit or at the poles, a top of the world.

clue.text: Red partly rolled-up tights in, um, moccasins?

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters lie concealed within them
in a down entry, rolled up means turned to run from the bottom, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the T of tights through the double C of moccasins

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly describing tights tucked into moccasins, oddly called a red.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the letters sNISACCOMMUNISThgit give the answer starting from the last C of moccasins.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a long-standing informal term for a communist, from the colour of the revolutionary flag.

clue.text: Country dance shortly over

indicators.note: made short, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the conga is a Latin American line dance
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A rural dance that is soon finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country dance' looks like a folk dance, but country is the definition: CONGA cut short plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Congo is a nation in central Africa, the Republic of the Congo, with Brazzaville as capital.

clue.text: Fun quantity of acts?

blocks.note: first meaning: lively and full of amusement
second meaning: as much as a theatre piece with several acts holds, like a cupful

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up word on the pattern of handful or spoonful, hence the question mark; a play is made up of acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful describes a lively, light-hearted manner, which is what fun means used as an adjective.

clue.text: Golf course ignoring opening signs

indicators.note: to ignore the opening is to skip the first letter of the word

blocks.note: a links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A golf course that won't open its gates puts up notices.
explanation.walkthrough: LINKS without its first letter gives INKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink a contract is to put one's signature on it, so inks means signs in that verb sense.

clue.text: Only playing new material

indicators.note: letters at play are moved around freely, so they come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A shop assistant insisting they only stock fresh fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric used for stockings, ropes and clothing, so it is a material.

clue.text: My French/Arabian/Australian fixation

blocks.note: mon is French for my
an Omani comes from Oman on the Arabian peninsula
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A slash-separated list of someone's obsessions with France, Arabia and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomania is an obsessive preoccupation with one single subject or idea.

clue.text: Fury of king amid loss of power

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the royal letter goes inside

blocks.note: an outage is a power cut
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch rages in the middle of a blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is intense anger or indignation, a synonym for fury.

clue.text: Isolated second outbuilding of five, originally

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a hut is a small outbuilding
taken as written
the first letter of five

explanation.surface: A remote shed, the second of five originally built.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut off means cut off or separated from others, the same as isolated.

clue.text: Lay on sponsor with finale getting rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged says outright that the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on a sponsored event whose closing number is reshuffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay on' looks like a phrasal verb, but lay alone is the definition, the adjective meaning not of the clergy or not expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay person lacks specialist training, so lay as an adjective means amateur rather than expert.

clue.text: Bring back harvest location

blocks.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
a point is a specific location

explanation.surface: A call to restore the place where the harvest happens.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappoint someone is to give them their former post again, bringing them back into office.

clue.text: Gen Z member allegedly mixing up wolf and snake

indicators.note: mixing things up jumbles their order, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young person reportedly confusing two animals, a wolf and a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowflake is a disparaging slang term for a young person supposedly too easily offended; allegedly signals that it is a slur, not a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics call younger people snowflakes, implying they are fragile and oversensitive, which is why the definition says allegedly.

clue.text: Navy making safe getaway, barely

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for navy
earthing an electrical circuit connects it to the ground so it is safe

explanation.surface: Naval forces securing their escape by the skin of their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe getaway' reads as one phrase, but safe belongs with making: earthing makes wiring safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, a situation where disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: Supporter fatally injured with boots in game of soccer

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a fan is a supporter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football fan dies horribly while wearing boots during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Fantasy football is a game in which players pick imaginary teams of real footballers and score points from their performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasy football is a competition built around real soccer players, so it is literally a game of soccer.

clue.text: Perhaps slip if climbing tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going up from the bottom, so the small word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the elder is a tree bearing elderberries

explanation.surface: Someone might lose their footing when climbing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket position near the batsman, and the player stationed there is a fielder; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is one of the close catching positions in cricket, so the player in it is an example of a fielder.

clue.text: City break covering ground at first like Tokyo?

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before
to cover something is to wrap around it, so the break goes around the single letter

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
a rest is a break
the first letter of ground

explanation.surface: A city break that takes in the ground floor first, perhaps in Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City break' reads as a holiday, but the two words are separate pieces. The question mark marks Tokyo as an example of the biggest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater Tokyo is the most populous urban area in the world, so it is the biggest of all cities.

clue.text: P Mescal stripped to be lead in The Count of Monte Cristo?

definitions.text: lead in The Count of Monte Cristo?

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: mescal without its outer letters
the letter P written out in full as its name

explanation.surface: The actor Paul Mescal undressing to play the hero of Dumas's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Mescal is an Irish actor, which makes 'P Mescal' read as a name; the spelt-out letter comes after the stripped spirit, mescal being a Mexican agave liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Dantès, hero of the novel, breaks out of the Château d'If prison, so the lead character is a famous escapee.

clue.text: Star couple finally leaving Sulawesi

indicators.note: letters that leave a word are taken out of it

blocks.note: the final pair of letters
Celebes is the former name of the Indonesian island Sulawesi

explanation.surface: A famous duo finally departing an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: CELEBES loses its last two letters, the couple at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeb is an informal shortening of celebrity, a famous person, which is what a star is.

clue.text: President set up yard sale site

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up stands it on end so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A president organises a yard sale on a website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard sale' looks like one phrase, but yard is Y and sale site is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is the online auction and marketplace where people sell goods, so it is a website for sales.

clue.text: Less interesting compliment

blocks.note: first meaning: more dull or lifeless, the comparative of flat
second meaning: to praise someone, often insincerely

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings come from unrelated words that happen to share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull, so flatter is duller; to flatter someone is to praise or pay them a compliment.

clue.text: May's predecessor having trouble about image management

indicators.note: about means around, so the trouble wraps itself around the other piece

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble
PR, public relations, is the management of an image

explanation.surface: Theresa May's predecessor struggling with spin doctoring.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like Theresa May, whose predecessor as Prime Minister was David Cameron, but it is the month.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the month that comes directly before May in the calendar.

clue.text: Tibetan backing a country like Germany

indicators.note: going backwards, the string of letters is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
Mali is a country in West Africa
à la means in the style of
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A Tibetan supports a nation that resembles Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: AMALIALAD reversed gives DALAILAMA; 'backing' looks like supporting, but it means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, so he is a famous Tibetan.

clue.text: Rear end of doctor is trapped in A&E

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
something trapped in another thing is held inside it

blocks.note: the last letter of doctor
A&E is the hospital accident and emergency department
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's backside gets stuck in the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear end' reads as a backside, but rear alone is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to bring them up, and to raise children means the same.

clue.text: Money back for abandoning villain

indicators.note: the villain abandons a small word, which is taken out of it

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
a reprobate is a wicked person

explanation.surface: Getting a refund for walking out on a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but supplies PRO, which is removed from REPROBATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund of money already paid, such as a tax rebate.

clue.text: Sign to stop Conservative welcoming Islamophobic organisation

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the organisation goes inside

blocks.note: the right is the conservative side of politics
the EDL, English Defence League, is a far-right anti-Islam street movement in Britain

explanation.surface: A political message urging the Conservatives to stop embracing anti-Muslim extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign to stop Conservative' reads as a protest banner, but the definition ends at stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light at a traffic signal instructs drivers to halt, so it is a signal to stop.
